issues.body: The document still says that nothing else in the tree pulls a Radix primitive. The reproduction proves only that every installed @radix-ui package belongs to the radix-ui barrel's transitive closure; it does not inspect reverse dependency edges and therefore cannot exclude another lockfile package also depending on one of those same primitives. This is materially the same minor finding as round 3 and does not undermine the reported closure sizes or byte partition.
issues.fix_hint: Remove the exclusivity claim, or extend the reproduction to scan dependency edges from all lockfile package entries and report non-barrel reverse dependents. Retain the exact-set assertion as evidence that the barrel accounts for every installed @radix-ui package.
issues.title: Closure equality still does not establish exclusive dependency provenance

verdict.summary: The round-3 minor wording overreach remains: equality between the barrel's transitive closure and the installed @radix-ui package set does not prove exclusive reverse-dependency provenance. The script never scans dependencies of packages outside that closure, so another package could also depend on a Radix primitive already present in the same set. This does not affect the closure sizes, used-versus-unused byte calculation, or the upstream recommendation, and no blocker or major correctness, soundness, test-validity, or security issue is present.
